a-brief-bible-history-a-survey-of-the-ol.title: A Brief Bible History: A Survey of the Old and New Testaments
a-brief-bible-history-a-survey-of-the-ol.creator: Boyd, James Oscar; Machen, J. Gresham
a-brief-bible-history-a-survey-of-the-ol.description: This book surveys the history of God's redeeming grace. It reviews Old Testament history, disclosing the stream of God's redeeming purposes flowing down through the older times. It reviews New Testament history, disclosing the broadening and deepening of that purpose for us men and for mankind in our Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ and his Church. The chapters included in this book appear also as...

arxiv-2101-07729.title: On a classical solution to the Abelian Higgs model
arxiv-2101-07729.creator: N. Mohammedi
arxiv-2101-07729.description: Abstract A particular solution to the equations of motion of the Abelian Higgs model is given. The solution involves the Jacobi elliptic functions as well as the Heun functions. 1 Introduction The search for analytical solutions to the classical equations of motion of field theories which are of relevance to certain domains of physics is of great interest.

arxiv-2105-08166.title: Variation of the Nebular Dust Attenuation Curve with the Properties of Local Star-forming Galaxies 2021 Variation of the Nebular Dust Attenuation Curve with the Properties of Local Star-forming Galaxies – References
arxiv-2105-08166.creator: Saeed Rezaee, Naveen Reddy, Irene Shivaei, Tara Fetherolf, Najmeh Emami, A. A. Khostovan
arxiv-2105-08166.description: Abstract We use a sample of 78,340 78,340 star-forming galaxies at z ≃ 0.04 − 0.1 z\simeq 0.04-0.1 from the SDSS DR8 survey to calculate the average nebular dust attenuation curve and its variation with the physical properties of galaxies.

arxiv-2204-02382.title: Down but not out: properties of the molecular gas in the stripped Virgo Cluster early-type galaxy NGC 4526 Facilities: ALMA, CARMA, IRAM
arxiv-2204-02382.creator: Lisa M. Young, David S. Meier, Alison Crocker, Timothy A. Davis, Selçuk Topal
arxiv-2204-02382.description: Abstract We present ALMA data on the 3mm continuum emission, CO isotopologues ( 12 CO, 13 CO, and C 18 O), and high-density molecular tracers (HCN, HCO + , HNC, HNCO, CS, CN, and CH 3 OH) in NGC 4526.

arxiv-2204-04410.title: THERMAL AND MAGNETIC FIELD STRUCTURE OF NEAR EQUATORIAL CORONAL HOLES
arxiv-2204-04410.creator: Hiremath, K. M. and Hegde, M
arxiv-2204-04410.description: Abstract We use full-disk, SOHO/EIT 195 Å \AA calibrated images to measure latitudinal and day to day variations of area and average photon fluxes of the near equatorial coronal holes. In addition, energy emitted by the coronal holes with their temperature and strength of magnetic field structures are estimated.

arxiv-2207-09029.title: Tens to hundreds of keV electron precipitation driven by kinetic Alfvén waves during an electron injection
arxiv-2207-09029.description: Abstract Electron injections are critical processes associated with magnetospheric substorms, which deposit significant electron energy into the ionosphere. Although wave scattering of < 10 <10 keV electrons during injections has been well studied, the link between magnetotail electron injections and energetic ( ≥ 100 \geq 100 keV) electron precipitation remains elusive.

arxiv-2207-11132.title: Proactive Distributed Emergency Response with Heterogeneous Tasks Allocation
arxiv-2207-11132.creator: Justice Darko \affilnum 1 and Hyoshin Park \affilnum 2
arxiv-2207-11132.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Justice Darko \affilnum 1 and Hyoshin Park \affilnum 2. Traditionally, traffic incident management (TIM) programs coordinate the deployment of emergency resources to immediate incident requests without accommodating the interdependencies on incident evolutions in the environment. However, ignoring inherent interdependencies on the evolution of incidents in the environment while making current deployment decisions is shortsighted, and the resulting naive deployment strategy can significantly worsen the overall incident delay impact on the network.

arxiv-2309-12862.title: Associative Transformer
arxiv-2309-12862.creator: Yuwei Sun, Hideya Ochiai, Zhirong Wu, Stephen Lin, Ryota Kanai
arxiv-2309-12862.description: Abstract Emerging from the pairwise attention in conventional Transformers, there is a growing interest in sparse attention mechanisms that align more closely with localized, contextual learning in the biological brain. Existing studies such as the Coordination method employ iterative cross-attention mechanisms with a bottleneck to enable the sparse association of inputs.

arxiv-2401-12102.title: Shear Layers and Plugs in the Capillary Flow of Wormlike Micellar Gels
arxiv-2401-12102.creator: Ronak Gupta, Masoud Daneshi, Ian Frigaard, Gwynn J. Elfring
arxiv-2401-12102.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Ronak Gupta, Masoud Daneshi, Ian Frigaard, Gwynn J. Elfring. Wormlike micellar solutions formed by long-chained zwitterionic surfactants show gel-like rheology at room temperature and have recently been found to exhibit other complex and interesting rheological features. We study the dynamics of these wormlike micellar gels in a pipe-flow scenario using optical coherence tomography-based velocimetry and report the existence of plug flows with strong wall slip and non-parabolic velocity profiles for different surfactant concentrations and imposed flow rates.

arxiv-2403-10911.title: Efficient Diffusion-Driven Corruption Editor for Test-Time Adaptation
arxiv-2403-10911.creator: Yeongtak Oh ∗, Jonghyun Lee ∗, Jooyoung Choi, Dahuin Jung, Uiwon Hwang †, Sungroh Yoon †
arxiv-2403-10911.description: Abstract Test-time adaptation (TTA) addresses the unforeseen distribution shifts occurring during test time. In TTA, performance, memory consumption, and time consumption are crucial considerations. A recent diffusion-based TTA approach for restoring corrupted images involves image-level updates. However, using pixel space diffusion significantly increases resource requirements compared to conventional model updating TTA approaches, revealing limitations as a TTA method.

arxiv-2403-11963.title: Transfer Learning Beyond Bounded Density Ratios Thanks: ∘ Department of Statistics and Data Science, Yale University; † Department of Computer Science, Yale University. ⋆ Institute of Foundations of Data Science, Yale University; Email: {alvertos.kalavasis, ilias.zadik, manolis.zampetakis}@yale.edu
arxiv-2403-11963.creator: Alkis Kalavasis ⋆ , Ilias Zadik ∘,⋆ and Manolis Zampetakis †,⋆
arxiv-2403-11963.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Alkis Kalavasis ⋆ , Ilias Zadik ∘,⋆ and Manolis Zampetakis †,⋆. We study the fundamental problem of transfer learning where a learning algorithm collects data from some source distribution P P but needs to perform well with respect to a different target distribution Q Q . A standard change of measure argument implies that transfer learning happens when the density ratio d ​ Q / d ​ P dQ/dP is bounded.

arxiv-2408-16518.title: An Interpretable and Crosslingual Method for Evaluating Second-Language Dialogues
arxiv-2408-16518.creator: Rena Gao, Jingxuan Wu, Carsten Roever, Xuetong Wu, Jing Wu, Long Lv, Jey Han Lau
arxiv-2408-16518.description: Abstract We analyse the cross-lingual transferability of a dialogue evaluation framework that assesses the relationships between micro-level linguistic features (e.g. backchannels) and macro-level interactivity labels (e.g. topic management), originally designed for English-as-a-second-language dialogues. To this end, we develop CNIMA ( C hinese N on-Native I nteractivity M easurement and A utomation), a Chinese-as-a-second-language labelled dataset with 10K dialogues.

arxiv-2502-15633.title: RGB-Only Gaussian Splatting SLAM for Unbounded Outdoor Scenes
arxiv-2502-15633.creator: Sicheng Yu, Chong Cheng, Yifan Zhou, Xiaojun Yang, Hao Wang
arxiv-2502-15633.description: Abstract 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) has become a popular solution in SLAM, as it can produce high-fidelity novel views. However, previous GS-based methods primarily target indoor scenes and rely on RGB-D sensors or pre-trained depth estimation models, hence underperforming in outdoor scenarios. To address this issue, we propose a RGB-only gaussian splatting SLAM method for unbounded outdoor scenes—OpenGS-SLAM.

arxiv-2511-12773.title: On planar sections of the dodecahedron
arxiv-2511-12773.creator: Andreas Thom
arxiv-2511-12773.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Andreas Thom. In the analysis of three-dimensional biological microstructures such as organoids, microscopy frequently yields two-dimensional optical sections without access to their orientation. Motivated by the question of whether such random planar sections determine the underlying three-dimensional structure, we investigate a discrete analogue in which the ambient structure is the vertex set of a Platonic solid and the observed data are congruence classes of planar intersections.

pmc-10621091.title: Clinical predictors and significance of adherent periadrenal fat in laparoscopic adrenalectomy
pmc-10621091.creator: Erkan Olcucuoglu, Samet Senel, Emre Uzun, Kazim Ceviz, Huseyin Gultekin, Hasan Batuhan Arabaci, Antonios Koudonas, Cevdet Aydin
pmc-10621091.description: BackgroundAdrenalectomy requires the anatomic preparation of the adrenal gland in the fat-rich retroperitoneal space. In the literature, it was shown that the retroperitoneal fat area affects surgical outcomes in laparoscopic adrenalectomy (LA). Besides the quantity of retroperitoneal fat, its qualitative properties play hypothetically a significant role in the safety profile and perioperative parameters of LA.

pmc-10748574.title: Diagnostic Accuracy of Conventional Ankle CT Scan With External Rotation and Dorsiflexion in Patients With Acute Isolated Syndesmotic Instability
pmc-10748574.creator: Joao Carlos Rodrigues, Adham do Amaral e Castro, Laercio Alberto Rosemberg, Cesar de Cesar Netto, Alexandre Leme Godoy-Santos
pmc-10748574.description: Category:Ankle; SportsIntroduction/Purpose:Syndesmotic injury in an athletic population is associated with a prolonged ankle disability after an ankle sprain and often requires a longer recovery than a lateral collateral ligament injury. Although several imaging tests are available, diagnosing syndesmotic instability remains challenging.

pmc-11392147.title: Commentary on: Predictive value of NT-proBNP and hs-TnT for outcomes after pediatric congenital cardiac surgery
pmc-11392147.creator: Xinlei Fu, Shilong Meng, Xiating Huang, Siwen Chen
pmc-11392147.description: The authors mainly conducted a prospective analysis of 1015 hospitalized children with congenital heart disease (CHD) who needed surgery in a tertiary center. Blood samples were taken 6 h after operation to detect the levels of N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) and high-sensitivity troponin T (hs-TnT) to predict the occurrence of postoperative adverse events.

pmc-11430960.title: Work Motivation: A Wall That Not Even the COVID-19 Pandemic Could Knock Down: Research Article
pmc-11430960.creator: Patrik M Bogdán, Miklós Zrínyi, Ildikó Madarász, Lívia Tóth, Annamária Pakai, Daniele Giansanti
pmc-11430960.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). The emergence of the coronavirus pandemic in 2020 posed a new challenge, imposing extraordinary physical and psychological burdens on healthcare workers, clearly exacerbating and intensifying career abandonment. Objectives: The aim of our study was to explore the motivating factors among nurses serving during the coronavirus pandemic that they considered important in their profession despite the mental and physical stress brought about by the pandemic.

pmc-11465588.title: Newcastle disease virus enhances the antitumor efficacy of Doxorubicin in a cervical cancer mouse model
pmc-11465588.creator: Aezam Rasekhi Kazeruni, Nahid Babaei, Hadi Esmaeili Gouvarchin Ghaleh, Abbas Doosti, Mahdieh Farzanehpour
pmc-11465588.description: Background and aimsCervical cancer (CC) is a common cancer among women, often treated with Doxorubicin (Doxo). Research is underway to explore the use of oncolytic virus (OV) therapy as a means to improve drug efficacy and enhance the immune system’s tumor-fighting capabilities.

pmc-11598617.title: Efficacy of a New Multivalent Vaccine for the Control of Bovine Respiratory Disease (BRD) in a Randomized Clinical Trial in Commercial Fattening Units
pmc-11598617.creator: Mariona Tapiolas, Marta Gibert, Carlos Montbrau, Ester Taberner, Marina Solé, Héctor Santo Tomás, Ainhoa Puig, Ricard March
pmc-11598617.description: A new multivalent vaccine (DIVENCE®), containing live gE/tk double-gene-deleted BoHV-1, live-attenuated BRSV, inactivated PI3, and BVDV-1, and BVDV-2 recombinant proteins, has been designed to protect cattle against the main viral pathogens associated with bovine respiratory disease (BRD). The aim of this study was to demonstrate the efficacy of DIVENCE® against BRD in field conditions.

pmc-11633718.title: First‐in‐human microelectrode recordings from the vagus nerve during clinical vagus nerve stimulation
pmc-11633718.creator: Mikaela Patros, David G. S. Farmer, Kegan Moneghetti, Matteo M. Ottaviani, Shobi Sivathamboo, Hugh D. Simpson, Terence J. O'Brien, Vaughan G. Macefield
pmc-11633718.description: IntroductionVagus nerve stimulation (VNS) is an effective treatment for people with drug‐resistant epilepsy. However, its mechanisms of action are poorly understood, including which nerve fibers are activated in humans during VNS in typical clinical settings and which are required for clinical efficacy.

pmc-12575628.title: Spatiotemporal modelling and monitoring of harmful algal blooms using IoT in Lake Victoria Basin Kenya
pmc-12575628.creator: Jacob Okello Okomo, Eunice Nduati, Fridah Kirimi
pmc-12575628.description: The escalating global concern of harmful algal blooms (HABs) in aquatic environments, poses significant challenges in the context of sustainable development goals (SDGs). The impacts of HABs extend beyond increased waterborne diseases, causing high aquaculture mortality, diminished aesthetic appeal, elevated drinking water treatment costs, and negative effects on tourism and gross domestic product (GDP).

pmc-12580655.title: The Impact of Lifestyle Counseling by Family Physicians on the Management of Hypertension in Primary Care Settings: A Systematic Review
pmc-12580655.creator: Fahad Ali A Alsahli, Atheer Suliman Alanazi, Salwa Eiad Atassi, Saied Yaser Sharif, Rinad Yaser Sharif, Nour Eddin Imad Alzayed, Hassan Ali Albaggal, Ahmed Almalki, Rashed Mishary Alshammari
pmc-12580655.description: Hypertension continues to be one of the most important avoidable risk factors for cardiovascular disease and early death. Many patients, especially in primary care settings, continue to have inadequate blood pressure control despite the availability of effective pharmaceutical medications. Fundamental tactics for avoiding and treating hypertension include dietary adjustments, greater physical activity, weight control, lowering salt intake, and quitting smoking.

pmc-13372837.title: Digital Mental Health Interventions in Obesity Management: A Systematic Review and Evidence-Based Recommendations
pmc-13372837.creator: Gloria Marchesi, Giada Rapelli, Michelle Semonella, Alessia Bruzzese, Martina Molinaro, Gerhard Andersson, Gianluca Castelnuovo, Giada Pietrabissa
pmc-13372837.description: BackgroundObesity is a complex condition encompassing behavioral, psychological, and physiological factors, frequently associated with elevated mental health burden. Digital Mental Health Interventions (DMHIs) have emerged as promising tools to enhance accessibility, personalization, and scalability of psychological care in obesity management. However, evidence on their effectiveness across delivery modalities and outcomes remains fragmented.

pmc-13455057.title: Glucagon‐like peptide‐1 receptor agonist‐based regimens compared with metformin‐based regimens for preventing cardiovascular disease in adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus
pmc-13455057.creator: Sana Ahmed, Sandra P McCollin, Arturo Martí-Carvajal, Monica Akus, David W Baron, Sara Abdul Razzaq, Paige Scudder, Elizabeth J Honigsberg, Saifuddin Nasir, Kangning Peng, Shayesteh Jahanfar
pmc-13455057.description:
A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). ObjectivesThis is a protocol for a Cochrane review (intervention).
